set.body:
THE ADDITIVE DECOMPOSITION IS ASSERTED WITH EXACT EQUALITY IN THREE PLACES AND IS NOT EXACT IN FLOATING POINT. Measured residual on ordinary data: 1.387779e-17.

WHERE:
  vignettes/introduction.Rmd:87   identical(effect$total, effect$coherent + effect$configuration)
  tests/testthat/test-workflow.R:35-36   expect_equal(..., tolerance = 0)
  tests/testthat/test-views.R:44-45      expect_equal(..., tolerance = 0)

identical() is the strictest of the three - it fails on any bit difference at all.

MEASURED. 8 features, 3 conditions, 3 runs, searchlights(2.01), seed 53:

  max abs (total - (coherent + configuration))   1.387779e-17
  all(diff == 0)                                 FALSE
  all.equal at tolerance 1e-12                   TRUE

So the identity holds to machine precision and fails exact equality.

WHY, and it is not a defect in the mathematics. The docs state configuration is DERIVED as total minus coherent, which is what makes the decomposition stable across reruns - and that claim is true and worth keeping. But in floating point, coherent + fl(total - coherent) does not always round-trip to total. It does when no rounding occurs, which depends on the magnitudes involved. The fixtures these three assertions run on happen to produce values where it does.

THE RISK IS IN TWO DIRECTIONS.

For a user: introduction.Rmd:87 is a check a reader can run on their own data. On data where rounding bites, identical() returns FALSE and the vignette's own consistency check appears to fail. A reader who has been told this is an exact additive split will conclude the package is broken, and the failure will look like it is about the decomposition rather than about floating point.

For the project: two test assertions at tolerance = 0 are fixture-dependent. They pass today because of the specific numbers in those fixtures. A BLAS change, a compiler change, a different platform, or an unrelated edit that perturbs the arithmetic order would break them, and the breakage would point at the decomposition rather than at the assertion.

Note this is NOT the same as the 45 other tolerance = 0 assertions in the suite, most of which are legitimate - reading a stored block back should be bitwise identical, and asserting that is right. The distinction is that those assert an IDENTITY OF STORAGE, whereas these three assert an IDENTITY OF ARITHMETIC that floating point does not guarantee.

FIX: assert the decomposition at a small nonzero tolerance - 1e-12 is already used elsewhere in the same files and passes here with room to spare. Keep the prose claim that configuration is derived by subtraction, since that is what actually prevents drift across reruns. Change identical() at introduction.Rmd:87 in particular, since it is the one a reader will run.

TIMING: introduction.Rmd is being edited right now under the p0 release slice, and line 87 is in the rewritten section. Cheapest to fix while the file is open."
set.title: The additive decomposition is asserted with exact equality in three places but is only exact to 1.4e-17
